Mathematics is largely about finding pat.body: Mathematics is mostly about finding patterns. It also asks why patterns exist. You can see patterns in nature, homes and schools. To compare fractions, first change them.body: To compare fractions, first use equivalent fractions. Make the denominators the same. Then compare the numerators. To add fractions, make the fractional units the same. Add the numerators. Keep the denominator. To subtract fractions, use the same denominator. Then subtract the numerators. Write the answer in lowest terms when needed. In Sanskrit, a fraction was called bhinna. It means broken. Bhaga and an sha meant a part or piece.
To compare fractions, first change them.explanation: These steps help you compare, add and subtract fractions.

Different figures show different kinds o.body: Different figures show different kinds of symmetry. Some have a line of symmetry. They have no angle of symmetry. Others have an angle of symmetry. They have no line of symmetry. Some have both. Fans, flowers and wheels show rotational symmetry. A circle matches itself after any rotation. Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry.
Different figures show different kinds o.explanation: A figure can show different kinds of symmetry.

Prime factorisation means writing a numb.body: Prime factorisation writes a number as a product of prime numbers. For 56, it is 2 × 2 × 2 × 7. The order of the prime factors does not matter. Every number greater than 1 has a prime factorisation. But 1 does not. The prime number 7 has the prime factorisation 7. Two numbers are co-prime when they have no common prime factors.
Prime factorisation means writing a numb.explanation: Prime factors help us compare numbers step by step.
keyPoints: Prime factorisation is a product of prime numbers.
The prime factorisation of 56 is 2 × 2 × 2 × 7.
Co-prime numbers have no common prime factors.

Regular polygons have all sides and all angles equal.

Rotational symmetry means an object look.body: Rotational symmetry means a shape looks the same after it turns. It turns around one point that does not move. This point is the centre of rotation. The paper windmill has rotational symmetry. When it turns 90° about its centre, it looks the same. Its symmetry angles are 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°. It has no line of symmetry.
Rotational symmetry means an object look.explanation: These ideas help you find rotational symmetry.

An angle can be compared by placing one.title: Compare angles and make turning arms
An angle can be compared by placing one.body: You can compare two angles by placing one over the other. This is called superimposition. The corner of an angle is its vertex. The vertices must overlap. Then you can see which angle is smaller or larger. Equal angles have matching corners and overlapping arms. Equal angles need the same amount of turn. A see-through circle helps you compare angles. Its centre must sit on the angle's vertex. To make turning arms, use two straws and a paper clip.
An angle can be compared by placing one.explanation: First put the angles on top of each other. Then check their corners and arms.

Number lines help you see how numbers si.body: A number line helps you see numbers. Negative numbers are to the left of zero. Smaller numbers are to the left of bigger numbers. In a bank passbook, a credit means money.title: Understanding Positive and Negative Numbers
In a bank passbook, a credit means money.body: In a bank passbook (a book that shows your money), a credit means money added. A debit means money taken out. Credits can be positive. Debits can be negative. Some banks let a balance go negative. Then the bank may charge interest or a fee. For heights, sea level is 0 metres. Above sea level is positive. Below sea level is negative. Temperature is measured in Celsius. At 0°C, water is at its freezing point.
In a bank passbook, a credit means money.explanation: These signs help you read bank money, heights and temperature.
keyPoints: Credits can be positive, and debits can be negative.
Heights above sea level are positive, and below are negative.
Celsius is the unit for measuring temperature.
